narrative: Material PL1__MA42A342 shows regular continuous demand (CV=0.22) with a statistically significant declining trend over the observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.74) with a bimodal distribution suggesting two distinct replenishment modes, which drives the safety stock requirement above the current SAP level. An (r,Q) fixed-order-quantity policy is recommended with safety stock raised to 2,386 units and reorder point set at 5,669 units to achieve the 95% service level target.
warnings: Declining demand trend detected (p<0.001) — re-validate annual demand projection in Q1 2027
Lead time CV=0.744 indicates unstable supply; bimodal distribution suggests two replenishment modes
7 outliers winsorized including one extreme spike of 4,932 units

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is regular and near-continuous (CV=0.22, 100% non-zero days), making a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. The EOQ-derived order quantity of 9,665 units balances ordering and holding costs, while the reorder point absorbs lead-time uncertainty. The high lead-time CV warrants a safety stock based on the combined demand-and-lead-time variance formula.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Capacity constraint does not bind: SS(2,386) + OQ(9,665) = 12,051 well below max_storage_units(33,513). No service degradation from capacity. If safety stock were raised further (e.g., to target 99% SL), capacity would still allow it.
